rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
rules.requirement: In most residential buildings older than 15 years, landlords cannot raise rent by more than 5% plus the local cost-of-living increase, or 10%, whichever is lower, in a 12-month period.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property/tenancies subject to subdivision (a); generally covers multifamily rental units not otherwise exempted (e.g., buildings over 15 years old, not deed-restricted affordable housing, not dormitories, not mobilehomes).
rules.exemptions: Mobilehome homeowner tenancies; units constructed within the last 15 years (rolling); deed-restricted affordable housing; certain dormitories.
rules.penalty: Civil liability to tenant for injunctive relief, damages equal to overcharge, attorney's fees/costs in court's discretion, and up to treble damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent, or malicious violations; AG, city attorney, or county counsel may also enforce and seek injunctive relief; action barred after 3 years from accrual.
rules.quoted_span: This section shall apply to all rent increases subject to subdivision (a) occurring on or after March 15, 2019, except as provided in subdivision (i).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is deed-restricted/regulated affordable housing or a dormitory

rules.conflict_note: A secondary provision (subdivision (h)) also references a March 15, 2019 to January 1, 2020 transition window, and a parallel transition window exists for February 18, 2021 to January 1, 2022 in another subsection, suggesting amendments over time; exact current numeric cap (e.g., 8.9% for Aug 2024-July 2025 per LA city page) is set via CPI formula each year, not a fixed figure in the statute text itself.
